summary: MISSION RELICS is an interactive space archaeology experience that brings the story of humanity’s abandoned equipment beyond Earth to life. Visitors explore the Moon, Mars, and deep space, discovering ten historical spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments left behind after their missions. Through interactive 3D models, archival NASA photographs, planetary environments, and evidence-based investigation pages, the project explains what each relic was designed to do, what science it enabled, and what remains today. MISSION RELICS addresses the challenge by turning mission history into an engaging educational journey for school-age space enthusiasts and the wider public. It connects real mission records and historical evidence with immersive exploration, helping visitors understand the engineering, discoveries, and legacy of space exploration.
details:
MISSION RELICS is an interactive 3D educational experience designed around the idea of planetary archaeology: exploring the human-made objects left behind beyond Earth and understanding the science and engineering behind them.

How it works

Visitors begin an exploration journey through three environments: the Moon, Mars, and deep space. They can browse ten relics, open individual investigation files, view archival photographs, and inspect available 3D models from different angles. Each investigation presents the object's operational purpose, historical milestones, scientific importance, discoveries, and mission outcome.

The ten featured relics

Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1), Apollo 12 ALSEP, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Pioneer 10, Apollo 12 Lunar Module Intrepid, Surveyor 3, Viking 1, and InSight.

Data and scientific integrity

The project uses NASA 3D resources, NASA and JPL archival photographs, NASA mission records, and historical technical documentation. Its guiding principle is “No Source, No Claim.” Official models, modified assets, and reconstructed models are clearly distinguished. Four relics use procedural reconstructions based on historical technical documentation where a suitable standalone official 3D model was not available. The MER rover inspection model uses official NASA VTAD geometry with recompressed textures for web delivery.

Technology

The experience is built with React, Vite, TypeScript, Three.js, and Tailwind CSS. Three.js powers the 3D environments, models, lighting, and interactive inspection. The project includes bilingual Arabic and English interfaces, responsive layouts, and optimized model levels of detail.

Impact

MISSION RELICS aims to make space exploration history more accessible and memorable by connecting real mission evidence with interactive storytelling. It encourages learners to explore the engineering and scientific legacy of missions rather than simply read about them.
